title: Python environments and notebooks
learning_objectives: Use isolated environments, reproducible notebooks and a terminal workflow.
concepts: An environment isolates dependencies; a notebook keeps code and outputs in cells but execution order can hide state. uv can manage environments and lock dependencies; pip installs packages into the active interpreter.
worked_example: Create a Python 3.11 environment, install NumPy and restart the kernel before running all cells.
common_pitfall: Installing into the wrong interpreter or relying on stale notebook variables.

exercise.task: Create an environment, run a notebook from a fresh kernel and record Python/package versions.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: The notebook runs top-to-bottom without manual state; the interpreter matches the environment.

title: Python data types, control flow and functions
learning_objectives: Write clear functions using lists, dictionaries, loops and comprehensions.
concepts: Functions encapsulate transformations. Mutable lists and dictionaries can be modified in place; tuples are immutable containers. Type hints document expected inputs but do not enforce them at runtime.
worked_example: Turn a list of measurement records into a dictionary of counts by category.
common_pitfall: Mutable default arguments can retain state across calls.

exercise.task: Implement a count-by-category function handling empty input and missing labels.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Empty input returns an empty dictionary; repeated calls are independent.

title: NumPy arrays, broadcasting and vectorization
learning_objectives: Manipulate multidimensional arrays and reason about shapes.
concepts: An ndarray stores homogeneous values; broadcasting aligns dimensions from the right when sizes match or one is 1. Vectorized operations avoid Python loops and exploit compiled kernels.
worked_example: Normalize each feature of a matrix using column means and standard deviations.
common_pitfall: Dividing by zero or silently broadcasting along the wrong axis.

exercise.task: Standardize a 3-column matrix including a constant column, preserving its shape.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Nonconstant columns have near-zero mean and unit variance; the constant column remains finite.

title: Pandas, data cleaning and EDA
learning_objectives: Inspect, join and summarize tabular data without leaking labels.
concepts: DataFrames associate named columns with rows. Missingness, duplicates, types and join cardinality affect downstream analysis. Exploratory data analysis (EDA) uses summaries and plots to discover patterns, not to establish causation.
worked_example: Inspect a customer table, flag missing ages, join transactions by customer ID and plot label frequency.
common_pitfall: Many-to-many joins can unexpectedly multiply rows; test-set exploration can bias model selection.

exercise.task: Create a data-quality report with missing counts, duplicate keys and label distribution.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report row counts before and after joins and identify nonunique keys.

title: Git, testing and reproducible experiments
learning_objectives: Track code and test deterministic data transformations.
concepts: Git tracks source changes; dependency locks and data/model versions record experimental context. Unit tests verify small functions, while integration tests cover interfaces. Random seeds improve repeatability but do not guarantee identical GPU computation.
worked_example: Commit a feature transformer and test empty, missing and valid values with pytest.
common_pitfall: Committing credentials or assuming seeds alone guarantee reproducibility.

exercise.task: Write three tests for a numerical feature transformer and document a run command.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Tests pass independently; secrets are not in the repository.

title: Linear algebra: vectors, matrices and dot products
learning_objectives: Explain shapes, matrix multiplication and similarity.
concepts: A vector is an ordered set of coordinates; matrix multiplication composes linear transformations. Dot products combine magnitude and alignment, while cosine similarity normalizes by vector norms.
worked_example: Calculate scores Xw+b for a batch with shape (n,d) and weights (d,).
common_pitfall: Confusing elementwise multiplication with matrix multiplication or ignoring zero norms.

exercise.task: Compute batch scores by hand for two rows and verify with NumPy.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Scores match and output shape is (2,).

title: Eigenvalues, SVD and projections
learning_objectives: Interpret dimensionality reduction as projection onto useful directions.
concepts: Eigenvectors preserve direction under a square linear transform; singular value decomposition factors a rectangular matrix into orthogonal directions and singular values. PCA projects centered data onto directions with greatest variance.
worked_example: Approximate a small matrix using its largest singular value and compare reconstruction errors.
common_pitfall: PCA components depend on scaling and do not necessarily preserve predictive information.

exercise.task: Reconstruct a matrix with ranks 1 and 2; calculate Frobenius error.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Rank-2 error is no larger than rank-1 error.

title: Probability, distributions and Bayes rule
learning_objectives: Reason about conditional probabilities and uncertainty.
concepts: Conditional probability measures an event given observed information. Bayes rule updates a prior with a likelihood and normalizes by evidence. Bernoulli, binomial and normal distributions model different types of random variables.
worked_example: A rare condition has a positive test; combine sensitivity, specificity and prevalence to calculate posterior probability.
common_pitfall: Confusing P(test positive given condition) with P(condition given test positive).

exercise.task: Use prevalence 1%, sensitivity 90% and specificity 95% to calculate posterior.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Posterior is about 15.4%, not 90%.

title: Statistics, sampling and confidence intervals
learning_objectives: Distinguish population parameters, sample estimates and uncertainty.
concepts: A statistic summarizes a sample; sampling variability describes how it changes across samples. Bootstrap resampling approximates estimator uncertainty under appropriate sampling assumptions. A frequentist confidence interval has coverage under repeated sampling, not a posterior probability for one fixed interval.
worked_example: Bootstrap a mean from independent observations and estimate a percentile interval.
common_pitfall: Ignoring dependence, selection bias or nonrepresentative samples.

exercise.task: Generate bootstrap intervals for sample sizes 20 and 200 from the same distribution.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Explain why larger samples generally yield narrower intervals.

title: Calculus, gradients and optimization
learning_objectives: Use derivatives, chain rule and gradient descent.
concepts: A derivative measures local sensitivity; gradients collect partial derivatives. Gradient descent subtracts a learning-rate-scaled gradient from parameters. The chain rule propagates derivatives through composed operations.
worked_example: Minimize (w-3)^2 using updates w = w - lr*2*(w-3).
common_pitfall: A learning rate that is too large can overshoot or diverge.

exercise.task: Compare trajectories for learning rates 0.1, 0.9 and 1.1.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Identify convergence, oscillation and divergence using loss values.

title: Information theory and numerical stability
learning_objectives: Explain entropy, cross entropy, KL divergence and stable log calculations.
concepts: Entropy measures uncertainty of a distribution; cross entropy penalizes predicted probabilities under a target distribution. KL divergence measures distribution mismatch and is asymmetric. Log-sum-exp stabilizes exponential calculations.
worked_example: Compare cross entropy for correct-class probabilities 0.9 and 0.1.
common_pitfall: Taking log(0) or applying softmax twice before a logits-based loss.

exercise.task: Compute negative log likelihood for both probabilities and explain the penalty.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: The 0.1 prediction has the higher loss; use stable log handling.

title: ML problem framing and baselines
learning_objectives: Translate a business objective into a supervised, unsupervised or reinforcement learning problem.
concepts: Supervised models learn from targets; unsupervised methods discover structure; reinforcement learning learns decisions from rewards. A simple baseline establishes whether complexity is justified. Define the prediction time, unit and consequence of errors.
worked_example: For churn prediction, define the observation window, target window and a majority-class baseline.
common_pitfall: Choosing an algorithm before defining the target or using information unavailable at prediction time.

exercise.task: Write a problem statement for demand forecasting with an explicit baseline and business metric.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Prediction horizon, input availability, split and cost of errors are explicit.

title: Train, validation, test and leakage
learning_objectives: Create representative splits and detect leakage.
concepts: Training fits parameters, validation selects configurations, and test estimates final generalization. Preprocessing must be fit within training folds. Time, entity and group boundaries often matter more than random splitting.
worked_example: Split patient-level measurements by patient, not individual row.
common_pitfall: Feature leakage from future data, repeated entities or target-derived columns.

exercise.task: Design splits for transactions from repeat users and for chronological demand data.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: No user overlap where required; test timestamps follow train timestamps for forecasting.

title: Preprocessing and feature pipelines
learning_objectives: Build imputers, encoders and scalers inside a reproducible pipeline.
concepts: Imputation handles missingness; one-hot encoding maps categories to indicators; scaling changes numerical magnitude. ColumnTransformer applies different transforms by column and Pipeline keeps transformations together with the estimator.
worked_example: Combine median imputation, standardization and one-hot encoding for mixed customer features.
common_pitfall: Unknown categories at inference or fitting preprocessing using the whole dataset.

exercise.task: Build a pipeline and predict a row with a missing number and unseen category.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Prediction succeeds with the same feature schema; fit uses training only.

title: Linear and polynomial regression
learning_objectives: Fit continuous targets and understand residuals and model assumptions.
concepts: Ordinary least squares minimizes squared residuals. Polynomial features add nonlinear basis functions while coefficients remain linear. Residual diagnostics reveal systematic errors; extrapolation can be unreliable.
worked_example: Predict house prices and plot residuals against fitted values.
common_pitfall: High-degree polynomials can overfit; correlation is not causal effect.

exercise.task: Fit degrees 1, 3 and 10 and compare validation RMSE.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Select the model by validation performance, not lowest training error.

title: Logistic regression and classification thresholds
learning_objectives: Interpret logits, probabilities and decision thresholds.
concepts: Logistic regression maps a linear score to a probability using the sigmoid for binary outcomes. Training often minimizes log loss; deployment chooses a decision threshold based on error costs.
worked_example: Change a fraud threshold from 0.5 to 0.2 and observe recall and false alarms.
common_pitfall: Treating probabilities as calibrated without checking or optimizing accuracy for rare positives.

exercise.task: Plot precision and recall for several thresholds and pick one for a review capacity.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Decision threshold is justified by validation costs, not by test outcomes.

title: k-nearest neighbors, naive Bayes and SVM
learning_objectives: Compare distance-based, probabilistic and margin-based classifiers.
concepts: kNN predicts using nearby samples; naive Bayes factorizes features conditionally on class; SVM optimizes a margin and may use kernels. Their inductive biases and scaling behavior differ.
worked_example: Compare all three on a standardized small classification dataset.
common_pitfall: Unscaled features dominate distances; kernel SVM can be expensive on large data.

exercise.task: Cross-validate three models using identical folds and report score and fit time.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Preprocessing is inside folds and trade-offs are documented.

title: Decision trees and random forests
learning_objectives: Explain recursive splitting, impurity and bagging.
concepts: A tree greedily partitions feature space using impurity or loss reduction. A random forest aggregates trees trained on resampled data and random feature subsets, reducing variance compared with many individual trees.
worked_example: Train a shallow tree and random forest on a nonlinear classification task.
common_pitfall: Unconstrained trees memorize training data; impurity importance can favor high-cardinality features.

exercise.task: Compare train and validation scores across tree depths and forest sizes.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report the generalization gap and a stable configuration.

title: Gradient boosting: XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost
learning_objectives: Compare sequential boosting with bagging and tune regularization.
concepts: Boosting builds an additive model by fitting successive learners to loss gradients or related targets. Learning rate, tree complexity and iterations trade bias, variance and computation. Libraries differ in categorical handling and histogram strategies.
worked_example: Train a histogram gradient boosting baseline before trying external libraries.
common_pitfall: Using early stopping on test data or encoding categories inconsistently.

exercise.task: Compare sklearn histogram boosting and one external booster on the same split.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Log validation metric, runtime and chosen iteration count.

title: Regularization, feature selection and bias-variance
learning_objectives: Control model complexity and explain underfitting and overfitting.
concepts: L1 penalties can produce sparse coefficients; L2 shrinks coefficients. Feature selection reduces dimensionality but must be part of training folds. Bias is systematic approximation error; variance reflects sensitivity to the sample.
worked_example: Compare Ridge and Lasso across penalty strengths on correlated features.
common_pitfall: Selecting features using all targets before cross-validation leaks information.

exercise.task: Plot learning curves and validation error for several penalty strengths.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Identify high bias or high variance and propose one intervention.

title: Classification, regression and ranking metrics
learning_objectives: Select metrics based on task and operating constraints.
concepts: Precision measures positive prediction correctness; recall measures positive coverage. ROC-AUC evaluates ranking across thresholds, while PR curves highlight rare-positive trade-offs. MAE and RMSE measure regression errors; nDCG rewards relevant ranked results near the top.
worked_example: Compare two fraud systems with equal accuracy but different minority recall.
common_pitfall: AUC does not identify an operating threshold and accuracy can hide minority failures.

exercise.task: Calculate confusion metrics and choose a metric for fraud review, demand forecast and search ranking.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Metric choice matches business costs and includes subgroup analysis.

title: Cross-validation and hyperparameter search
learning_objectives: Estimate model-selection performance and optimize efficiently.
concepts: Cross-validation rotates validation folds; grouped or time-aware variants respect dependencies. Grid/random search explores parameter configurations; nested CV separates tuning from performance estimation. Bayesian optimization chooses promising candidates adaptively.
worked_example: Tune forest depth and leaf size with grouped folds.
common_pitfall: Repeatedly tuning against the final test set invalidates it.

exercise.task: Run randomized search and report mean, standard deviation and final holdout performance once.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Split strategy and search budget are recorded.

title: Imbalanced learning, calibration and uncertainty
learning_objectives: Evaluate probabilities and handle rare classes responsibly.
concepts: Class weights alter training loss; resampling changes the training distribution. Calibration compares predicted probability with observed frequency and can use held-out sigmoid or isotonic fitting. Prediction intervals or conformal methods quantify uncertainty under stated assumptions.
worked_example: Use class weighting for rare events, then compare reliability diagrams before and after calibration.
common_pitfall: Oversampling before splitting leaks duplicate or related rows; calibration requires separate data or folds.

exercise.task: Compare precision-recall, Brier score and calibration curves on a natural-prevalence holdout.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report threshold, prevalence and calibration approach.

title: Interpretability, fairness and error analysis
learning_objectives: Investigate failures and assess subgroup performance.
concepts: Permutation importance measures score changes when a feature is shuffled; SHAP attributes model output relative to a baseline. Explanations are not causal evidence. Fairness metrics can conflict, so choose context-appropriate definitions and examine subgroups.
worked_example: Compare recall and false-positive rate across relevant consented groups and investigate proxy features.
common_pitfall: Treating feature attribution as causality or reporting only aggregate accuracy.

exercise.task: Produce an error slice report with subgroup sizes, metrics and limitations.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Small groups are flagged; proposed mitigations are evaluated on validation data.

title: Clustering: k-means, hierarchical and DBSCAN
learning_objectives: Discover structure and compare clustering assumptions.
concepts: k-means minimizes squared distance to centroids; hierarchical clustering builds nested groups; DBSCAN uses density connectivity and can mark noise. Scale and geometry strongly affect results.
worked_example: Cluster synthetic crescent-shaped data using k-means and DBSCAN.
common_pitfall: Treating clusters as true labels or relying on a single internal score.

exercise.task: Compare silhouette scores and visual structure across algorithms.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Explain which geometries and parameter choices fit the data.

title: Dimensionality reduction: PCA, t-SNE and UMAP
learning_objectives: Choose linear reduction versus neighborhood visualization.
concepts: PCA is a linear projection; t-SNE and UMAP construct nonlinear embeddings emphasizing aspects of neighborhood structure. Low-dimensional plots may distort global distances, density and cluster separation.
worked_example: Reduce handwritten digit vectors to two dimensions and compare stability across seeds.
common_pitfall: Interpreting all distances and cluster sizes in t-SNE as meaningful.

exercise.task: Compare PCA explained variance and multiple nonlinear embeddings.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Document seed, settings and visualization limitations.

title: Anomaly detection and novelty detection
learning_objectives: Identify unusual observations with scarce labels.
concepts: Isolation Forest isolates observations via random splits; one-class methods estimate a normal region. Anomaly scores require thresholds and operational review; anomalies may be benign or reflect data quality.
worked_example: Detect rare sensor spikes with a model trained on normal historical data.
common_pitfall: Training on future incidents or assuming every anomaly is malicious.

exercise.task: Evaluate precision at a fixed daily alert budget using labeled anomalies.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report false positives and sensitivity to changing baseline behavior.

title: Time series, forecasting and backtesting
learning_objectives: Use time-aware validation, lag features and forecasting baselines.
concepts: Forecasting predicts future values with temporal dependence, seasonality and trends. Rolling-origin backtests preserve order; features must be available at forecast creation. Seasonal naive and exponential smoothing provide useful baselines.
worked_example: Forecast weekly demand using last week's value and lagged features.
common_pitfall: Random splitting or calculating rolling features that include future observations.

exercise.task: Build three expanding-window backtests and compare MAE to seasonal naive.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: All prediction dates follow their training data; forecast horizon is constant.

title: Recommendation and learning to rank
learning_objectives: Understand collaborative, content-based and ranking systems.
concepts: Collaborative filtering learns from user-item interactions; content-based methods use item features. Two-stage systems retrieve candidates then rank them. Offline evaluation must avoid future interactions and account for exposure bias.
worked_example: Recommend items by user-item similarity, then evaluate recall@k on held-out events.
common_pitfall: Random negative sampling can misrepresent unseen relevance and cold-start performance.

exercise.task: Compare popularity baseline with nearest-neighbor recommendations.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report recall@k for warm and cold-start segments separately.

title: Causal inference and experimentation
learning_objectives: Distinguish prediction, intervention and causal effects.
concepts: Random assignment supports estimating treatment effects under assumptions; observational causal inference requires identification assumptions such as exchangeability and positivity. Confounders affect treatment and outcome. A/B tests need prespecified metrics and stopping rules.
worked_example: Design an experiment comparing two recommendation interfaces.
common_pitfall: Conditioning on post-treatment variables or repeatedly peeking at p-values without adjustment.

exercise.task: Specify unit of randomization, primary outcome, guardrail metrics and analysis plan.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Plan addresses interference, missing data and statistical uncertainty.

title: Tensors, autograd and PyTorch fundamentals
learning_objectives: Create tensors, compute gradients and move data between devices.
concepts: Tensors have shape, dtype and device. Autograd records differentiable operations to compute gradients. Gradients accumulate by default and must be cleared between optimizer updates.
worked_example: Differentiate y=(x**2).sum() for a vector with requires_grad enabled.
common_pitfall: In-place mutation of tracked tensors or mixing CPU and GPU tensors.

exercise.task: Compute an analytic gradient and compare with autograd.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Gradient equals 2*x within tolerance.

title: Perceptrons, MLPs and activation functions
learning_objectives: Build a neural network with nonlinear hidden layers.
concepts: An affine layer maps x to Wx+b. Nonlinear activations such as ReLU or GELU allow composition to model nonlinear functions. Without nonlinearities, stacked affine layers remain affine.
worked_example: Train a two-layer MLP on XOR or a small tabular classification dataset.
common_pitfall: Applying sigmoid to logits before BCEWithLogitsLoss or using incompatible target shape.

exercise.task: Compare a linear model with an MLP on XOR.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: MLP can fit XOR; linear baseline cannot perfectly separate it.

title: Forward pass, backpropagation and loss functions
learning_objectives: Trace gradients through a small neural network.
concepts: Forward propagation produces predictions and loss; backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute parameter gradients. Cross entropy for multiclass logits, BCE for binary and MSE for regression require appropriate target formats.
worked_example: Compute gradients for a tiny scalar two-layer network and compare to autograd.
common_pitfall: Detaching a tensor breaks its gradient path; incorrect logits/target shapes can silently mislead.

exercise.task: Hand-derive gradients for a scalar linear prediction and squared loss.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Analytic and autograd gradients agree.

title: Optimizers, initialization and learning-rate schedules
learning_objectives: Choose SGD, momentum and AdamW; stabilize training.
concepts: SGD updates using minibatch gradients; momentum smooths updates; AdamW adapts coordinate step sizes with decoupled weight decay. Initialization and schedules influence optimization stability and convergence.
worked_example: Compare AdamW and SGD on the same architecture and seed budget.
common_pitfall: Confusing L2 regularization with decoupled weight decay for adaptive optimizers.

exercise.task: Train short runs at several learning rates and log loss curves.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Choose based on validation and stability rather than a single training curve.

title: Datasets, DataLoaders and training loops
learning_objectives: Build explicit training and evaluation loops.
concepts: Datasets define sample access; DataLoaders batch and optionally shuffle. A training loop runs forward, loss, backward and optimizer step. Evaluation uses model.eval() and disables gradient recording.
worked_example: Train a classifier on generated features with batches and validation metrics.
common_pitfall: Forgetting eval mode changes dropout and batch normalization behavior.

exercise.task: Implement train_epoch and evaluate functions with sample-weighted losses.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Training changes weights; evaluation does not; batch sizes are handled correctly.

title: Normalization, dropout and early stopping
learning_objectives: Reduce overfitting and manage activation distributions.
concepts: Batch normalization uses batch statistics in training and running statistics in evaluation; layer normalization normalizes within examples across selected dimensions. Dropout randomly masks activations during training. Early stopping selects a checkpoint from validation.
worked_example: Train a model with dropout and compare train/eval outputs on identical inputs.
common_pitfall: Evaluating with dropout active or selecting checkpoints using test loss.

exercise.task: Compare baseline, dropout and weight decay using validation curves.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Restore the best validation checkpoint and report test once.

title: Mixed precision, GPUs and distributed training
learning_objectives: Explain memory/performance trade-offs and distributed data parallelism.
concepts: Mixed precision uses lower precision where safe while retaining stability for sensitive calculations. Data parallelism replicates models and synchronizes gradients; model parallelism partitions computation or parameters. Profiling reveals actual bottlenecks.
worked_example: Estimate memory used by parameters, gradients and optimizer state before scaling training.
common_pitfall: Assuming lower precision is always faster or forgetting effective batch size changes.

exercise.task: Compare throughput and validation loss on available hardware; if CPU-only, calculate memory estimates.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report precision, device, batch size, throughput and numerical anomalies.

title: CNN foundations and receptive fields
learning_objectives: Calculate convolution output shapes and explain weight sharing.
concepts: Convolution slides kernels over spatial input with shared weights. Stride, padding and dilation control output dimensions and receptive field. Pooling summarizes neighborhoods and may reduce resolution.
worked_example: Apply a 3x3 edge kernel and calculate output dimensions for stride 2.
common_pitfall: Confusing channels-first and channels-last layout or shrinking spatial dimensions unexpectedly.

exercise.task: Design a CNN and calculate the shape after each layer before running it.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Computed shapes match actual tensor shapes.

title: RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs and sequence modeling
learning_objectives: Explain recurrence and gating for ordered data.
concepts: RNNs update hidden state from current input and previous state. LSTM and GRU gates help control information flow and mitigate some long-range gradient issues. Padding and masks matter for variable-length sequences.
worked_example: Predict the next symbol in a toy sequence with a GRU.
common_pitfall: Shuffling tokens within a sequence or treating padding as real observations.

exercise.task: Train a small GRU on synthetic sequences and compare to a naive baseline.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Evaluate on sequences not used in training and explain failure cases.

title: Attention and transformers
learning_objectives: Explain queries, keys, values, masking and positional information.
concepts: Scaled dot-product attention computes softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V. Multihead attention captures different projections. Transformers combine attention, feedforward layers, residuals, normalization and position information; causal masks prevent attending to future tokens.
worked_example: Compute attention weights for three tokens and compare masked versus unmasked output.
common_pitfall: Mask polarity errors and quadratic attention memory for long sequences.

exercise.task: Implement small causal attention with a triangular mask and test future-token invariance.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Changing future tokens does not alter earlier outputs.

title: Encoder, decoder and encoder-decoder architectures
learning_objectives: Choose architecture for classification, generation and sequence translation.
concepts: Encoders typically use bidirectional context for representations; decoder-only language models use causal attention for next-token generation; encoder-decoder models condition decoding on encoded input. Architecture choice affects masking and training objectives.
worked_example: Compare BERT-like classification, GPT-like generation and T5-like summarization.
common_pitfall: Assuming every transformer has identical masking or can generate text autoregressively.

exercise.task: Diagram the three architectures and label attention connections and objectives.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Each diagram correctly indicates access to future input and target tokens.

title: Transfer learning, embeddings and self-supervised learning
learning_objectives: Reuse learned representations and distinguish pretraining from adaptation.
concepts: Transfer learning adapts a pretrained model through frozen feature extraction or fine-tuning. Self-supervised learning constructs training signals from raw data, such as masked tokens or contrastive views. Embeddings map items into a representation space.
worked_example: Freeze a backbone, train a classification head, then selectively unfreeze layers.
common_pitfall: Training too aggressively can destroy useful pretrained features; domain shift can limit transfer.

exercise.task: Compare frozen and partially unfrozen models on a small validation set.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Log trainable parameters, data split and performance.

title: Autoencoders, VAEs and GANs
learning_objectives: Compare reconstruction and generative modeling objectives.
concepts: Autoencoders reconstruct inputs through a latent representation; VAEs learn probabilistic latents with reconstruction and KL terms. GANs train a generator against a discriminator in an adversarial objective.
worked_example: Train a small autoencoder and inspect reconstruction error and latent structure.
common_pitfall: A good reconstruction score does not guarantee useful generation; GANs may collapse modes.

exercise.task: Compare reconstruction on normal and shifted samples; explain how VAE sampling differs.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Show inputs, reconstructions and failure examples.

title: Diffusion and score-based generative models
learning_objectives: Explain forward noising and learned denoising.
concepts: Diffusion models corrupt data with noise according to a schedule and learn a reverse process or equivalent prediction target. Sampling iteratively denoises; conditioning guides generation. Latent diffusion operates in a learned compressed space.
worked_example: Add Gaussian noise at several steps and train a toy noise predictor.
common_pitfall: Confusing training noising with inference denoising or assuming fewer steps always preserve quality.

exercise.task: Visualize a simple noising schedule and compare denoising errors across timesteps.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Explain the trade-off between sampling compute and quality.

title: Reinforcement learning and preference optimization
learning_objectives: Understand policies, rewards, value functions and alignment objectives.
concepts: An agent interacts with an environment to optimize expected return. Value functions estimate future return; policy gradients optimize a parameterized policy. RLHF may use learned reward models; DPO directly optimizes preferences under its assumptions.
worked_example: Compare random and epsilon-greedy policies on a toy bandit; relate preferences to language-model adaptation.
common_pitfall: Reward hacking, biased preference data and conflating reward with real user value.

exercise.task: Implement a two-armed bandit and report cumulative regret across seeds.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Show exploration/exploitation effects and limitations.

title: Image representation, color spaces and OpenCV
learning_objectives: Read, inspect and convert images correctly.
concepts: Images are arrays of pixels with spatial dimensions and channels. OpenCV commonly reads color images in BGR order; RGB, grayscale and HSV serve different tasks. Data range and dtype affect arithmetic.
worked_example: Convert a BGR image to grayscale and HSV; inspect channel histograms.
common_pitfall: Displaying BGR as RGB or overflowing uint8 during arithmetic.

exercise.task: Create a synthetic color image, convert spaces and verify channel values.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Shapes and dtype are recorded; channel conversion is correct.

title: Filtering, edges and morphology
learning_objectives: Apply smoothing, gradients, thresholding and morphological operators.
concepts: Convolution filters alter local neighborhoods. Gaussian blur reduces high-frequency noise; Sobel and Canny detect edges; erosion and dilation change binary regions. Opening removes small foreground structures, closing fills small gaps.
worked_example: Clean a noisy binary mask and detect edges around a shape.
common_pitfall: Over-smoothing removes important detail; morphology depends on kernel and polarity.

exercise.task: Compare masks for multiple kernel sizes and quantify foreground area.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Preserve target shape while removing isolated noise.

title: Geometric transforms, calibration and features
learning_objectives: Estimate mappings and match local image structures.
concepts: Affine transforms preserve parallelism; homographies model planar projective mappings. Camera intrinsics and distortion parameters support calibration. ORB detects and describes local features for matching.
worked_example: Match features between a synthetic image and a rotated version, then estimate a homography with RANSAC.
common_pitfall: Homographies fail for many nonplanar scenes; feature matches can contain outliers.

exercise.task: Apply a perspective transform and quantify inlier matches or reprojection error.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Use robust estimation and report geometric assumptions.

title: Image datasets, augmentation and labeling
learning_objectives: Construct reliable train/validation splits and label contracts.
concepts: Augmentations simulate plausible variation such as crop, flip or lighting change. Labels must be transformed consistently with images for detection and segmentation. Group splits prevent leakage across near-duplicate frames or patients.
worked_example: Build transforms for classification and bounding boxes; split by video source.
common_pitfall: Applying random training augmentations to validation or flipping labels with directional meaning.

exercise.task: Create a dataset audit with class counts, duplicates, split groups and annotation examples.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Validation transforms are deterministic and label geometry remains consistent.

title: Image classification and pretrained CNNs
learning_objectives: Train and evaluate a transfer-learning image classifier.
concepts: ResNet uses residual connections to ease deep optimization; EfficientNet scales architecture dimensions systematically. Replace a pretrained classifier head and use model-specific normalization.
worked_example: Fine-tune a small pretrained model on an image dataset or use a synthetic offline baseline.
common_pitfall: Forgetting pretrained input normalization or evaluating only overall accuracy.

exercise.task: Compare a scratch CNN and pretrained backbone using the same split.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report macro F1, per-class confusion and inference time.

title: Object detection: boxes, IoU, NMS and mAP
learning_objectives: Understand detection outputs and evaluation.
concepts: A detector predicts bounding boxes, class scores and confidence. Intersection over union (IoU) measures box overlap; nonmaximum suppression removes redundant detections in many pipelines. Average precision integrates a precision-recall curve under matching rules; mAP averages specified AP values.
worked_example: Calculate IoU for two boxes and inspect duplicate detections after NMS.
common_pitfall: Mixing xyxy and xywh coordinates or comparing mAP computed under different IoU settings.

exercise.task: Implement IoU and class-aware NMS for a few predicted boxes.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover no overlap, exact match and different classes.

title: YOLO, Faster R-CNN, DETR and detection training
learning_objectives: Compare one-stage, two-stage and set-prediction detectors.
concepts: YOLO-style detectors typically predict dense detections in one pass; Faster R-CNN uses region proposals then classification/refinement; DETR treats detection as set prediction with matching. Accuracy, latency and small-object performance depend on setup.
worked_example: Benchmark a small detector with a fixed image size and a representative labeled set.
common_pitfall: Comparing published speed numbers from different hardware or resolution.

exercise.task: Train or fine-tune a detector on a small custom dataset; profile latency and mAP.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Record architecture, data license, image size, IoU settings and hardware.

title: Semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation
learning_objectives: Select segmentation types and metrics.
concepts: Semantic segmentation assigns a class per pixel; instance segmentation distinguishes objects of the same class; panoptic segmentation combines stuff and thing labels. Dice and IoU quantify mask overlap with stated averaging rules.
worked_example: Compare a predicted binary mask with ground truth and calculate Dice and IoU.
common_pitfall: Including ignored pixels in metrics or using bilinear interpolation for discrete labels.

exercise.task: Implement mask metrics and evaluate per-class scores on synthetic masks.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Tests include empty masks and documented empty-class conventions.

title: U-Net, Mask R-CNN, SAM and foundation vision models
learning_objectives: Compare segmentation architectures and prompting.
concepts: U-Net combines an encoder and decoder with skip connections; Mask R-CNN adds instance mask prediction to region-based detection; SAM-style models produce masks from prompts. Promptable models still need domain evaluation and possibly adaptation.
worked_example: Segment objects from point or box prompts and compare against labeled masks.
common_pitfall: Assuming promptable models are accurate for every domain or using unlicensed imagery.

exercise.task: Evaluate segmentation quality for difficult cases such as occlusion or small objects.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report per-case IoU and prompts; note domain limitations.

title: Video, optical flow and object tracking
learning_objectives: Process temporal frames and maintain object identities.
concepts: Optical flow estimates apparent motion; tracking links detections through time using motion and appearance. Kalman filters estimate state under uncertainty; assignment methods associate observations. Tracking metrics measure detection and identity continuity.
worked_example: Track moving shapes across frames with simple centroid matching.
common_pitfall: Ignoring frame-rate variation, occlusion or identity switches.

exercise.task: Create a synthetic video sequence with crossing objects and compare identity errors.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Document track creation/deletion and failure cases.

title: Vision transformers, CLIP and multimodal vision
learning_objectives: Explain patch embeddings, contrastive alignment and zero-shot vision.
concepts: Vision Transformers tokenize image patches and use attention. CLIP-style models align image and text embeddings through contrastive learning; zero-shot classification compares image embeddings with textual class descriptions.
worked_example: Compare class text prompts for a small image set and measure prompt sensitivity.
common_pitfall: Assuming zero-shot scores are calibrated or ignoring training-data bias.

exercise.task: Evaluate two prompt templates and inspect misclassified images.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report macro F1 and prompt sensitivity on a fixed split.

title: OCR, document AI, 3D and deployment
learning_objectives: Identify OCR pipelines, depth estimation and efficient vision inference.
concepts: OCR often combines text detection and recognition; document AI adds layout and structure. Depth can come from stereo geometry or learned models. Deployment uses batching, quantization and export formats such as ONNX; preprocessing must match training.
worked_example: Extract text from synthetic receipts and benchmark an exported classifier.
common_pitfall: Logging sensitive documents or ignoring coordinate transforms during resizing.

exercise.task: Build an OCR or image inference mini-pipeline with latency and error tests.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Return structured outputs, verify preprocessing parity and measure failures.

title: Generative AI landscape and LLM fundamentals
learning_objectives: Distinguish text, image, audio and multimodal generation and language-model training stages.
concepts: Autoregressive LLMs predict next tokens; pretraining learns broad statistical patterns; instruction tuning and preference optimization adapt behavior. Generative output is probabilistic and may be unsupported even when fluent.
worked_example: Compare a language-model completion, embedding lookup and classifier on a support task.
common_pitfall: Equating fluency with factual accuracy or assuming model knowledge is current.

exercise.task: Classify five business use cases by generation, retrieval or deterministic computation.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Explain when a non-generative solution is preferable.

title: Tokens, tokenizers and context windows
learning_objectives: Explain subword tokenization, special tokens, budgets and truncation.
concepts: Tokenizers convert text to integer IDs using schemes such as BPE, WordPiece or unigram. Special tokens represent boundaries or roles. Context limits include model-specific input and generated token accounting; token counts vary by model and language.
worked_example: Compare token counts of code, English and multilingual text with a chosen tokenizer.
common_pitfall: Counting words as tokens or truncating away required evidence and role markers.

exercise.task: Measure token counts for three strings and implement a context-budget check.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Use the actual model tokenizer and reserve space for output.

title: Decoding, sampling and inference constraints
learning_objectives: Compare greedy, temperature, top-k and top-p decoding.
concepts: Greedy chooses a highest-probability token; temperature rescales logits; top-k limits candidate count; top-p retains a probability mass. Stops, output limits and constrained decoding influence completion behavior. Determinism is not guaranteed across serving systems.
worked_example: Generate several responses under greedy and sampled settings and compare diversity.
common_pitfall: Using low temperature as a correctness guarantee or confusing top-p with top-k.

exercise.task: Record five generations per setting and compare format compliance and diversity.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Separate repeatability from factual accuracy.

title: Hugging Face Hub, Transformers and model selection
learning_objectives: Load tokenizers/models and inspect model cards and licenses.
concepts: The Hub distributes model artifacts and metadata; Transformers provides model and tokenizer APIs. A model card describes intended use, limits and evaluation, but should be verified. Choose base versus instruction model, context, memory and license.
worked_example: Load a small permitted model and use its tokenizer and generation config.
common_pitfall: Executing untrusted remote model code or assuming all licenses permit commercial use.

exercise.task: Compare three model cards for task fit, license, size and known limitations.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Document exact revision and do not enable remote code without review.

title: Zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot prompting
learning_objectives: Design examples for task specification and contextual generalization.
concepts: Zero-shot uses instructions without examples; one-shot supplies one demonstration; few-shot uses multiple representative examples. Examples guide output style and decision boundaries but do not guarantee deterministic inference or generalization.
worked_example: Classify support messages using zero, one and several examples and compare held-out accuracy.
common_pitfall: Example contamination, order sensitivity and assuming one-shot makes output deterministic.

exercise.task: Build a labeled holdout and compare all three prompt variants with fixed decoding settings.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report accuracy, format errors and example-selection criteria.

title: Structured output, few-shot schemas and Pydantic
learning_objectives: Validate generated objects at the application boundary.
concepts: Structured generation may use JSON schema constraints or tool arguments; few-shot examples illustrate semantic mappings. Pydantic validates typed Python objects, can reject extra fields and express constraints. Valid structure does not guarantee truthful content.
worked_example: Extract an invoice object with required currency, total and item fields.
common_pitfall: Accepting parseable JSON as factual truth or silently coercing invalid values.

exercise.task: Define a strict Pydantic schema and test malformed, missing and extra fields.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Invalid payloads fail safely; valid payloads serialize predictably.

title: Persona prompting, reasoning prompts and prompt injection
learning_objectives: Use role/context and concise reasoning artifacts without treating reasoning text as proof.
concepts: Persona prompts establish tone, audience and constraints, not genuine expertise. Chain-of-thought prompting is a research approach to eliciting intermediate reasoning; applications can instead request concise justification, verifiable calculations or structured plans. Untrusted content must remain data.
worked_example: Ask a tutor to return an answer plus a short evidence-based explanation, then test adversarial user text.
common_pitfall: Trusting a plausible explanation as evidence of correctness or exposing hidden reasoning or secrets.

exercise.task: Compare persona vs neutral prompts and test input that asks to ignore instructions.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Evaluate correctness and instruction adherence using external checks.

title: Prompt serialization: ChatML, Alpaca and INST
learning_objectives: Explain how messages become model-specific serialized token sequences.
concepts: ChatML-style formats use role delimiters; Alpaca-style templates often use Instruction/Input/Response sections; [INST]-style formats mark instruction boundaries in certain model families. Exact control tokens and role rules vary by tokenizer and model revision.
worked_example: Inspect tokenizer.apply_chat_template on system, user and assistant messages and compare conceptual templates.
common_pitfall: Manually applying the wrong template, duplicating special tokens or concatenating untrusted messages as instructions.

exercise.task: Render two actual model templates and identify role and generation markers.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Use the tokenizer's own template and document supported roles.

title: Prompt versioning, testing and context engineering
learning_objectives: Treat prompts and context as versioned software artifacts.
concepts: A prompt includes instructions, examples, retrieved evidence and output contracts. Context engineering selects, orders and truncates inputs; tests track behavior across model or prompt changes. Stable schemas and adversarial fixtures support regression testing.
worked_example: Version two prompts with a dataset of normal, ambiguous and injection attempts.
common_pitfall: Changing model and prompt simultaneously makes attribution difficult.

exercise.task: Create a prompt registry record with model revision, template hash and evaluation results.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Regression report compares one variable at a time and tracks cost and latency.

title: Embeddings, similarity and vector databases
learning_objectives: Understand dense retrieval and approximate nearest-neighbor search.
concepts: Embeddings represent text or images as vectors. Cosine, dot-product and Euclidean similarity rank candidates differently depending on normalization. Vector stores index embeddings with metadata and support filtering; examples include FAISS, Qdrant, Chroma and pgvector.
worked_example: Embed short documents and compare semantic search with exact keyword search.
common_pitfall: Mixing embedding models in one index or missing tenant filters.

exercise.task: Implement brute-force cosine retrieval, then compare one vector backend.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Record model, dimension, metric and metadata filter behavior.

title: RAG ingestion, chunking and indexing
learning_objectives: Build a reproducible retrieval-augmented generation ingestion pipeline.
concepts: RAG retrieves external evidence at inference. Ingestion parses, cleans, chunks, embeds and indexes source content with provenance. Chunk size and overlap affect recall, noise and cost. Incremental indexing needs stable document IDs and deletion handling.
worked_example: Chunk a small set of policy documents, preserving section headings and source IDs.
common_pitfall: Indexing private content without access metadata or dropping document boundaries.

exercise.task: Build a chunker with stable IDs and test document update/deletion behavior.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Chunks trace to source spans and old versions can be removed.

title: RAG retrieval, reranking and answer grounding
learning_objectives: Combine sparse, dense and hybrid retrieval with evidence-based generation.
concepts: Sparse search such as BM25 matches lexical terms; dense retrieval captures semantic similarity. Hybrid fusion combines signals; reranking scores candidate-query relevance more expensively. Answers should cite evidence and abstain when evidence is insufficient.
worked_example: Retrieve top candidates for an acronym query, rerank and build a bounded context.
common_pitfall: Using similarity as proof of factual support or citing sources not actually retrieved.

exercise.task: Measure recall@k before/after hybrid retrieval and manually inspect citations.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Answer cites only available source IDs and abstains on unanswerable queries.

title: RAG evaluation and retrieval diagnostics
learning_objectives: Separate retrieval quality, grounding and answer usefulness.
concepts: Retrieval metrics include recall@k, precision@k, MRR and nDCG; generation metrics include correctness, faithfulness and citation precision. Reference data and human review are necessary for reliable interpretation.
worked_example: Compare two chunk sizes on a golden query-document set and identify retrieval versus generation failures.
common_pitfall: Evaluating only final answer similarity can hide retrieval failure or unsupported claims.

exercise.task: Create ten answerable and five unanswerable queries and report retrieval and answer metrics.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Show per-query evidence and abstention behavior, not just averages.

title: Self-reflective RAG and Self-RAG
learning_objectives: Compare model-trained reflection signals with application-level grading loops.
concepts: Self-RAG is a research method using learned reflection tokens to control retrieval and critique generations. Application-level self-reflective RAG may instead use separate graders for evidence relevance, grounding and answer usefulness; these are related but not identical.
worked_example: Retrieve evidence, grade relevance, generate and run a grounding check before returning an answer.
common_pitfall: Calling any retry loop the original Self-RAG algorithm or trusting a self-grader without validation.

exercise.task: Implement a bounded grade-and-retry loop with a deterministic mock grader and evaluate false accepts.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Stop on max attempts and preserve evidence for every decision.

title: Corrective RAG (CRAG)
learning_objectives: Use retrieval-quality assessment to trigger corrective retrieval.
concepts: The CRAG research approach evaluates retrieved-document quality and triggers corrective actions, including knowledge refinement and possible external search. An application-inspired implementation may route to rewrite, alternate index or approved search when evidence is weak.
worked_example: Grade retrieval as strong, weak or ambiguous; route weak cases to a second trusted corpus.
common_pitfall: Sending sensitive queries to unapproved search or using corrective results without provenance.

exercise.task: Implement a three-way retrieval-quality router with an offline fallback corpus.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Route tests cover strong, weak, ambiguous and unavailable fallback cases.

title: Self-corrective RAG and iterative verification
learning_objectives: Design bounded correction of unsupported or incomplete answers.
concepts: Self-corrective RAG is a broad application pattern rather than a single universal algorithm. Verify claims against evidence, revise or retrieve again and stop when quality gates pass or budget is exhausted.
worked_example: Detect missing citation support in a generated answer and regenerate only unsupported claims.
common_pitfall: Infinite loops and a judge repeatedly approving its own hallucination.

exercise.task: Implement a verifier with max three attempts and an explicit abstain state.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: All runs terminate; unsupported claims are removed or flagged.

title: Agentic RAG and routing
learning_objectives: Allow a bounded agent to select retrieval tools and decompose queries.
concepts: Agentic RAG uses a model or controller to choose retrieval actions, sources or subqueries. It can support multi-hop questions, but introduces extra latency, cost and failure modes. Authorization must be enforced outside the model.
worked_example: Route a policy question to internal search and a product question to a catalog tool.
common_pitfall: Unbounded tool calls, cross-tenant retrieval or unnecessary agency for simple questions.

exercise.task: Compare deterministic routing with a bounded agent on a mixed question set.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report route accuracy, recall, tool count and cost proxy.

title: Tool calling and tool-use agent pattern
learning_objectives: Design typed, permissioned tool interfaces and handle errors.
concepts: A tool call is structured data requesting an external operation. The application validates arguments, authorizes execution, returns results and manages timeouts. Read and write tools have different risk profiles; side effects need idempotency and approvals.
worked_example: Expose a read-only inventory lookup with typed item ID and structured result.
common_pitfall: Executing arbitrary model-generated code or treating tool output as trusted instructions.

exercise.task: Implement a tool registry, argument validation and unknown-tool error handling.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Invalid and unauthorized calls do not execute; errors are structured.

title: ReAct, planning and action-observation loops
learning_objectives: Explain the interleaving of decisions, actions and observations.
concepts: ReAct is a research pattern interleaving reasoning with actions and environment observations. An application can expose concise action decisions and tool results rather than private reasoning traces. State, stop conditions and budgets control the loop.
worked_example: Use a controller to choose between lookup, calculator and final answer based on observations.
common_pitfall: Infinite repeated actions, stale observations and blindly following tool text.

exercise.task: Build a mock loop that stops after four actions or a valid final result.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Trace records action name, sanitized arguments, observation and termination reason.

title: Reflection and evaluator-optimizer agents
learning_objectives: Improve drafts using feedback and explicit acceptance criteria.
concepts: A reflection loop creates a candidate, critiques it against a rubric and revises. An evaluator-optimizer workflow separates generation from grading; a deterministic validator may be better for objective constraints. Bound iterations and compare with one-pass baseline.
worked_example: Generate a short summary, grade missing required facts, then revise once.
common_pitfall: Self-critique can reinforce errors and add unnecessary cost.

exercise.task: Build a mock rubric checker and compare one-pass versus iterative outputs.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Track improvement, revision count, failure rate and stop reason.

title: Multi-agent systems and orchestration
learning_objectives: Choose supervisor-worker, handoff and parallel specialist patterns.
concepts: Multiple agents can divide tasks or specialize tools; a supervisor coordinates routing and state, while handoff transfers responsibility. Coordination costs and inconsistent state can outweigh benefits. Shared contracts and permissions are necessary.
worked_example: A research coordinator delegates retrieval and verification to separate workers then merges evidence.
common_pitfall: Recursive delegation, conflicting writes and sharing unnecessary private context.

exercise.task: Implement a supervisor with two mock specialists and bounded fan-out.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Each worker has narrow tools; merge resolves conflicts and records provenance.

title: LangChain components and integration boundaries
learning_objectives: Use chat models, prompts, structured outputs, retrievers and tools as composable interfaces.
concepts: LangChain integrates providers, retrievers, messages and agent components. Separate domain logic from framework adapters so tests can use fakes and migration is easier. Keep configuration and secrets outside prompts.
worked_example: Build a prompt-to-model-to-validated-output pipeline with a mock model first.
common_pitfall: Tightly coupling business logic to provider-specific responses or using deprecated examples uncritically.

exercise.task: Implement an adapter and swap a fake for one configured model.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Tests run without network; provider failures return controlled errors.

title: LangGraph state, nodes, edges and sequential workflow
learning_objectives: Represent a workflow as typed shared state with deterministic transitions.
concepts: LangGraph represents stateful workflows as nodes and edges. Nodes return state updates; edges define transitions. A sequential workflow follows a known order and is appropriate when the steps are predictable.
worked_example: Build validate -> retrieve -> generate -> finish using typed state.
common_pitfall: Mutating shared state unexpectedly or placing unrelated data in the graph.

exercise.task: Create a two-node offline graph and test the final state.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Each node has a clear state contract and can be unit-tested.

title: LangGraph conditional and parallel workflows
learning_objectives: Route by state and merge independent branches safely.
concepts: Conditional edges choose a destination using state; parallel branches execute independent work and need reducers or explicit merge contracts for concurrent state updates. Fan-out and fan-in should be bounded.
worked_example: Route invalid inputs to rejection; run keyword and vector retrieval in parallel and merge IDs.
common_pitfall: Multiple branches updating the same state key without merge semantics.

exercise.task: Construct a mock router and two parallel branches with a deterministic reducer.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Both branches contribute exactly once; invalid routes terminate.

title: LangGraph iterative workflows, checkpointing and HITL
learning_objectives: Build bounded loops, resumable state and human approval gates.
concepts: Iterative graphs revisit nodes until a quality or budget condition; checkpointing persists graph state by thread. Human-in-the-loop interrupts pause at controlled points and resume with a decision. Side effects must be idempotent across replay.
worked_example: Pause a proposed write action for approval, then resume only if authorized.
common_pitfall: Re-executing a side effect on resume or storing secrets in checkpoint state.

exercise.task: Build a review gate and test approve, reject and resume cases.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: No write occurs before approval; duplicate resume does not duplicate side effects.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) fundamentals
learning_objectives: Explain host, client, server, tools, resources, prompts and transport.
concepts: MCP standardizes how AI applications connect to external context and capabilities. A host coordinates clients; servers expose tools, resources and prompts. Transport and authorization depend on deployment and protocol revision. MCP does not grant permission automatically.
worked_example: Design a server exposing read-only document search and a resource URI.
common_pitfall: Equating MCP with an agent framework or trusting every discovered capability.

exercise.task: Diagram host/client/server and define schemas and permissions for two capabilities.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Explain the difference between tool execution and resource access.

title: FastMCP server and client development
learning_objectives: Implement typed tools and test discovery and invocation.
concepts: FastMCP provides Python decorators and client abstractions for MCP. Typed function signatures expose tool schemas; resource and prompt definitions expose context or reusable templates. Local stdio is useful for development; remote deployments require transport-aware security.
worked_example: Implement a local add or catalog lookup tool with FastMCP and invoke using a client.
common_pitfall: Exposing filesystem or shell tools without restrictions, or assuming SDK and standalone FastMCP APIs are interchangeable.

exercise.task: Create a read-only server, list tools and test valid/invalid invocation.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Discovery works and validation rejects malformed arguments.

title: MCP security, remote deployment and interoperability
learning_objectives: Threat-model external servers and enforce least privilege.
concepts: Remote MCP servers need authenticated and authorized access, validated resource identifiers, timeouts and audit logging. Tool descriptions and results are untrusted content. Review server provenance, restrict outbound requests and pin protocol/library versions.
worked_example: Integrate a remote document server behind tenant-scoped permissions and explicit write approval.
common_pitfall: Token passthrough without audience validation, prompt injection and SSRF through arbitrary URLs.

exercise.task: Write a threat model and tests for cross-tenant requests and malformed resource IDs.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Unauthorized data is denied and logs omit secrets.

title: Memory taxonomy: working, factual, episodic and semantic
learning_objectives: Separate immediate context from persistent user or task memory.
concepts: Working memory is current context and state. Long-term semantic memory stores general knowledge or meaning, factual memory stores discrete facts and is often treated as a subset of semantic memory, and episodic memory records events or experiences. Procedural memory can store reusable actions or policies.
worked_example: Store a preference as a fact, a past support interaction as an episode and current task variables in working state.
common_pitfall: Treating every conversation as durable memory or conflating factual and semantic categories as universally disjoint.

exercise.task: Design a memory schema with type, source, timestamp, scope and expiry.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Each entry has an explicit purpose and retention decision.

title: Memory retrieval, summarization and vector storage
learning_objectives: Design memory read/write lifecycles and token-budgeted context.
concepts: Memory pipelines select candidates, resolve duplicates, store provenance, retrieve by relevance and recency, and inject only authorized context. Summaries compress history but may omit important details; vector search does not guarantee correct recall.
worked_example: Compare raw chat history, rolling summary and retrieved memory on a follow-up question.
common_pitfall: Stale preferences, accidental cross-user retrieval and treating retrieved memory as instructions.

exercise.task: Implement a scoped in-memory store with update and delete operations, then add vector retrieval.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Two users remain isolated; deleted entries no longer appear in results.

title: Mem0 and persistent agent memory
learning_objectives: Integrate a memory layer with a configurable LLM, embedder and vector backend.
concepts: Mem0 supports extraction, storage and retrieval of memory using configured models and vector stores. Application policy determines consent, scope, update rules and deletion. Evaluate memory precision, recall, freshness and false memories separately from answer quality.
worked_example: Add a user-authorized preference under a test user ID and retrieve it for a later query.
common_pitfall: Using defaults without understanding external data flow, retaining sensitive data or failing to remove stale memory.

exercise.task: Connect Mem0 in a sandbox or implement an adapter with a fake backend; test add/search/update/delete.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: User isolation and deletion behavior are verified; provider dependencies documented.

title: FastAPI, Pydantic and async inference APIs
learning_objectives: Expose validated inference endpoints with controlled errors.
concepts: FastAPI maps HTTP requests to typed Python handlers; Pydantic defines data contracts. Async I/O helps concurrent network-bound calls; blocking CPU/GPU operations may require workers or separate inference services. Authentication, limits and timeouts belong at service boundaries.
worked_example: Expose a typed prediction or chat endpoint and test malformed inputs.
common_pitfall: Blocking an async event loop, returning secrets in exceptions or accepting unbounded requests.

exercise.task: Build a FastAPI service with health and validated inference endpoints.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Tests cover success, invalid input, timeout and error responses.

title: Streaming responses: SSE, chunks and cancellation
learning_objectives: Stream incremental output safely and detect completion or failure.
concepts: Server-sent events use text/event-stream and framed events; clients should handle partial content, error and completion events. Provider streaming, application streaming and UI rendering are separate layers. Cancellation and backpressure limit wasted resources.
worked_example: Stream a mock token sequence using FastAPI StreamingResponse and detect disconnect.
common_pitfall: Assuming each chunk is valid JSON or leaking unsafe content before moderation completes.

exercise.task: Implement SSE events for delta, done and error and test a canceled client.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Events are framed correctly; cancellation stops unnecessary work.

title: LiteLLM gateway, routing and fallback
learning_objectives: Unify provider access and enforce gateway policies.
concepts: LiteLLM offers a Python SDK and proxy gateway with provider abstraction, routing, virtual keys, budgets and observability features. Retry/fallback policies must distinguish transient failures from invalid requests. Models and providers have different capabilities and token accounting.
worked_example: Route two configured model deployments behind a common alias and simulate rate limiting.
common_pitfall: Retrying non-idempotent side effects or switching models that do not support the required schema.

exercise.task: Create a gateway configuration template and test mock fallback behavior.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Log selected model, failure reason, latency and cost metadata without secrets.

title: Guardrails, prompt injection, privacy and HITL
learning_objectives: Create layered safety controls and approval workflows.
concepts: Input validation, output schema checks, tool authorization, PII handling, content policy checks and human review provide complementary defenses. Prompt injection treats untrusted content as attempted instructions; no single filter guarantees protection. Streaming may require buffering or incremental checks.
worked_example: Block unauthorized writes even when a model claims approval and mask sensitive fields in logs.
common_pitfall: Relying solely on an LLM judge or releasing unreviewed streamed content.

exercise.task: Threat-model an agent and build tests for injection, unauthorized actions and sensitive output.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Fail closed for protected actions; escalation and audit events are recorded.

title: Agent evaluation, datasets and LLM-as-judge
learning_objectives: Design reliable agent and LLM evaluation beyond final answer accuracy.
concepts: Evaluate task success, tool selection, arguments, trajectory, latency, cost, safety and human intervention. LLM-as-judge uses a model to score a rubric; position bias, verbosity bias and correlated errors require human calibration and deterministic checks where possible.
worked_example: Compare an answer judge with human labels and measure agreement on a held-out set.
common_pitfall: Using the same model as generator and uncalibrated sole evaluator or exposing private traces to judges.

exercise.task: Create a rubric with anchors, run pairwise comparisons in both orders and review disagreements.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report agreement, judge config and failure cases; do not use judge score alone.

title: DeepEval for LLM and agent regression tests
learning_objectives: Integrate metric-based evaluations into a test workflow.
concepts: DeepEval provides evaluation constructs for model outputs and various task-specific metrics. Use synthetic and human-authored cases, deterministic assertions for tool contracts and configured model judges for semantic metrics. Judge calls may incur cost.
worked_example: Create cases for grounded answers and unsupported claims using a configured evaluator.
common_pitfall: Confusing metric thresholds with universal quality standards or depending on live models for all unit tests.

exercise.task: Write an offline exact-match test and a separate opt-in DeepEval semantic test.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Offline CI works without keys; judge-backed checks log thresholds and model.

title: Ragas for RAG evaluation
learning_objectives: Measure retrieval and generation with appropriate reference data.
concepts: Ragas offers metrics for retrieval and answer assessment, with metric-specific required fields and judge/embedding dependencies. Use human-reviewed examples to calibrate and distinguish context recall, precision and faithfulness.
worked_example: Evaluate retrieval evidence against reference answers for a small question set.
common_pitfall: Using an unavailable reference field or comparing metrics across changed evaluator configurations.

exercise.task: Prepare a dataset with user input, retrieved contexts, response and reference; select appropriate metrics.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report per-metric required columns, model and sample-level failure analysis.

title: Promptfoo for prompt/model evaluation and red teaming
learning_objectives: Run test matrices across prompt/provider combinations and adversarial cases.
concepts: Promptfoo supports declarative evaluation configurations, provider/prompt matrices and assertions. Some checks are deterministic; judge-based assertions use a configured model. Security testing needs permission, scoped targets and non-sensitive fixtures.
worked_example: Evaluate two support prompts with regex/schema assertions and a rubric.
common_pitfall: Storing API keys in YAML or attacking systems without authorization.

exercise.task: Create a local evaluation configuration for normal and adversarial inputs with pass criteria.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report passing and failing cases and keep secrets in environment variables.

title: Observability, traces, evaluation gates and cost
learning_objectives: Make LLM applications measurable and govern releases.
concepts: Trace spans connect model calls, retrieval and tools; metrics include latency percentiles, token usage, cost, success and safety violations. Release gates compare quality and operational budgets against a baseline. Redact sensitive input/output and restrict trace retention.
worked_example: Compare two RAG versions by recall@k, grounded answer rate, p95 latency and token cost.
common_pitfall: Logging secrets or using aggregate metrics that hide high-risk failures.

exercise.task: Define an evaluation dashboard and a CI gate for four metrics with rollback criteria.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Each metric has dataset, threshold, owner and failure action.

title: Fine-tuning datasets, SFT and PEFT/LoRA
learning_objectives: Explain supervised adaptation and low-rank updates.
concepts: SFT trains on curated instruction-response examples. LoRA freezes base weights and learns low-rank updates to selected matrices, reducing trainable parameters. PEFT libraries implement adaptation; evaluate on a disjoint holdout and document base-model license.
worked_example: Inspect trainable parameter counts for a small model before and after applying LoRA.
common_pitfall: Training on benchmark answers, poor data formatting or assuming fine-tuning adds reliable current facts.

exercise.task: Create a small licensed instruction dataset, split it, configure LoRA and plan a baseline comparison.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Report trainable parameters, data provenance and validation metrics.

title: QLoRA, quantization, serving and model optimization
learning_objectives: Trade numerical precision, memory and quality deliberately.
concepts: QLoRA combines quantized frozen base weights with trainable adapters. Quantization reduces memory but may affect accuracy and requires compatible kernels. Serving optimizations include KV caching, batching, speculative decoding and runtime choices such as vLLM or llama.cpp.
worked_example: Compare memory estimates for FP16 and 4-bit weights before adapter overhead.
common_pitfall: Assuming four-bit storage equals complete runtime memory or every GPU supports every kernel.

exercise.task: Estimate weight and KV-cache memory and benchmark a compatible serving configuration if hardware is available.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Document hardware, model, quality, throughput and actual peak memory.

title: Multimodal LLMs, diffusion apps and fine-tuning decisions
learning_objectives: Select RAG, prompting, tools or adaptation for multimodal tasks.
concepts: Multimodal models process inputs such as images and text using modality encoders or joint representations. Image generation uses methods including diffusion. Prompting changes input behavior; RAG supplies evidence; tools perform actions; fine-tuning adapts learned behavior. Evaluate each modality and rights/privacy constraints.
worked_example: Build a document-question-answering design combining OCR, vision and text retrieval.
common_pitfall: Treating fine-tuning as a replacement for retrieval or submitting private images to unapproved providers.

exercise.task: Design a benchmark and choose an architecture for document QA versus image generation.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Justify modality, evidence source, model choice, and privacy controls.

title: Model packaging, APIs and Docker
learning_objectives: Package inference artifacts with reproducible dependencies and contracts.
concepts: A deployable model includes preprocessing, weights, schema, dependency metadata and version identifiers. Docker images isolate user-space runtime; non-root users, minimal base images and health probes reduce operational risk.
worked_example: Package a scikit-learn pipeline behind FastAPI and build a local container.
common_pitfall: Loading untrusted pickle/joblib artifacts or training on service startup.

exercise.task: Build a container and run a health check and prediction contract test.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Container runs without training or secrets baked into image.

title: MLflow, data versioning and experiment tracking
learning_objectives: Track dataset, parameters, metrics, artifacts and promotion decisions.
concepts: MLflow tracks experiment runs and model metadata; DVC or object-store versioning can track data artifacts. A registry can record model versions and promotion decisions. Reproducibility requires immutable references and environment metadata.
worked_example: Log two model runs and compare validation metrics and artifacts.
common_pitfall: Storing sensitive data in experiment metadata or promoting based on training score.

exercise.task: Track a baseline and candidate; record why one is promoted.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Runs include code/data identifiers and reproducible configuration.

title: CI/CD, continuous training and DevSecOps
learning_objectives: Build gates for data, models, services and dependencies.
concepts: CI validates source, data contracts, tests and model metrics; CD promotes approved artifacts. Dependency, secret and container scanning reduce supply-chain risk; continuous training requires data and quality gates. Use staged deployment and rollback.
worked_example: Create a pipeline with lint, unit tests, evaluation, dependency scan and approval before deploy.
common_pitfall: Automatically promoting a retrained model without comparing it to a baseline.

exercise.task: Design CI for a model service and simulate a failed quality threshold.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Failed tests or quality gates block release; artifacts are immutable.

title: Monitoring, drift, reliability and retraining
learning_objectives: Detect changes in inputs, behavior and operational health.
concepts: Data drift changes input distribution; concept drift changes the relationship between inputs and targets; label delays limit immediate accuracy monitoring. Track latency, errors, resource use and data quality; retrain only after validated diagnosis.
worked_example: Simulate a shifted feature distribution and monitor prediction scores.
common_pitfall: Treating every detected shift as concept drift or retraining automatically without verification.

exercise.task: Create drift and service alerts, escalation thresholds and a rollback plan.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Alerts have actionable ownership, context and known false-positive limitations.

title: Responsible AI, governance and security
learning_objectives: Build privacy, documentation and risk controls into AI lifecycle.
concepts: Governance covers data rights, consent, access, model cards, risk assessment, evaluation and incident response. Threat models include training-data poisoning, extraction, adversarial inputs and unauthorized agent actions. Requirements depend on jurisdiction and application.
worked_example: Create a model card and risk register for a support assistant with sensitive data.
common_pitfall: Assuming public data is always licensed for training or logging full user conversations.

exercise.task: Draft data inventory, model limitations, approval checkpoints and incident procedure.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Every risk has mitigation, owner and validation evidence.

title: Cloud architecture, scaling and deployment trade-offs
learning_objectives: Design a production AI workload with cost and reliability budgets.
concepts: Separate API, model serving, storage, queueing and observability. Batch processing favors throughput; online inference favors latency. AWS examples include S3, ECS/EKS, SageMaker and managed databases; equivalent services exist on other clouds.
worked_example: Design a RAG service with tenant-scoped retrieval, gateway and async ingestion queue.
common_pitfall: Overprovisioning GPUs, exposing indexes publicly or scaling without measurement.

exercise.task: Diagram architecture, forecast cost drivers and define rollback and recovery objectives.
exercise.acceptance_criteria: Architecture includes identity, encryption, limits, monitoring and failure isolation.
